expected.text: Same broken REPO_ROOT fallback as ao-update.sh: `$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]")/..` now resolves to `dist/assets` instead of the package root. This cascades into the SCRIPT_LAYOUT auto-detection at lines 34-38, which checks `$REPO_ROOT/package.json` and `$REPO_ROOT/dist/index.js` to identify package installs. With the wrong REPO_ROOT, neither file exists, so `SCRIPT_LAYOUT` defaults to `source-checkout` on a direct package-install invocation. The doctor then runs source-checkout checks (looking for `node_modules`, `packages/core/dist`, etc.) against the wrong root, producing spurious FAIL results on a healthy package install.

`handleGitUpdate` hardcodes `"npm-global"` as the fallback when `hasRepoScript("ao-update.sh")` returns false. `getUpdateCommand("npm-global")` returns `npm install -g @aoagents/ao@latest`, which silently converts a git source-checkout user to a global npm package install rather than directing them to rebuild with `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli build`. The correct fix would be an error message with a rebuild hint, not a method-switching npm install command.

`run_smoke_tests` references `$REPO_ROOT/packages/agent-orchestrator/bin/ao.js`, but that directory no longer exists — the wrapper package is at `packages/ao/bin/ao.js`. The smoke tests will always fail with a missing file error even on a healthy source checkout. This was present before the rename but the PR had the opportunity to fix it while touching this file, and the broken path now receives wider exposure since the script is bundled and more likely to be audited.
